name: Bubble Sort
description: Simple comparison-based sorting algorithm that repeatedly steps through the list, compares adjacent elements, and swaps them if they are in the wrong order. The pass through the list is repeated until the list is sorted.
aim: To sort an array by repeatedly comparing and swapping adjacent elements until the entire array is in ascending order. Uses an optimized version that stops early if no swaps were made in a pass (adaptive behavior).
howItWorks: Start from the first element and compare each pair of adjacent elements
If the left element is greater than the right, swap them
After each pass, the largest unsorted element 'bubbles up' to its correct position
Repeat for n-1 passes (where n is array length)
Stop early if a complete pass makes no swaps (already sorted)

time.bestCase: Array is already sorted — only one pass needed with no swaps
time.averageCase: Random data — roughly n²/2 comparisons on average
time.worstCase: Array is sorted in reverse — maximum number of swaps needed

complexity.spaceDescription: In-place sorting — no extra array needed

realWorld: Educational purposes — simplest sorting algorithm to visualize and teach
Nearly sorted data — performs close to O(n) when array is almost ordered
Small datasets — acceptable performance for arrays with fewer than 50 elements
Embedded systems — minimal memory footprint due to O(1) space complexity
whenToUse: Data is already nearly sorted and n is small
Simplicity is more important than raw performance
You need a stable sort with minimal code
alternatives: Use Quick Sort for large random datasets — O(n log n) average time
Use Merge Sort when stability with better performance is needed
Use Insertion Sort for nearly sorted small arrays (better constant factors)
Use Counting Sort for integers within a limited range — O(n + k)
